failures.criterion: A session that upgrades from the old plugin's core path to this release's consumer delivery is shown everything stored while it was away — the review's critical finding, and the move every Legion worker makes when its image is re-pinned
failures.evidence: A followed issue topic is still lost across the upgrade, and today's released plugin does not lose it. I drove it live, with tooling I wrote and committed for it (1d2d2849, `scripts/e2e/envoy-session-delivery.sh --resume-plugins-from <rev>`: both sessions start on the plugins built from <rev> and are resumed, after the window's events are stored, on this checkout's). Command: `LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN=… ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=… bash scripts/e2e/envoy-session-delivery.sh --disruptions a --resume-plugins-from 96a7e5ea9099aabf25dc8b524177b6f73df4eab5` (main's tip, pi-envoy 13.5.1 and claude-envoy 1.0.0). Result, twice, with different marker nonces (LDTbd47 and LDT4b61): `ENVOY SESSION DELIVERY: FAIL`; the two comments on the followed issue `notifications.dispatch.issue.LIVE-1`, published while both sessions were killed, counted 0 in both transcripts, while every agent event (the Dispatch message and the listener send) and every role event (the listener publish and the core publish) counted 1. Both sessions had the issue topic in their registry entry before the kill (`topics: [notifications.agent.<id>, notifications.dispatch.issue.LIVE-1, …]`). Three states of the same window, same stack, same pod: old plugin throughout (`--plugins-from 96a7e5ea`) → the two comments counted 1 and 1, the role events 0, which is today's behaviour and the core path's known limit; new plugin throughout (the round's full run) → all 60 markers of six windows counted 1; old plugin upgraded to new at the resume → the comments 0, the role events 1. So the upgrade loses what the release it replaces recovers, and it is a regression at the exact transition, not a pre-existing gap. Where to look: the seeded resume (`seededResume` in packages/envoy-client/src/consumer-delivery.ts) and the first consumer's start for a followed topic — the unit tests that cover H1 seed only the agent subject (`subjects: { [AGENT]: { since, after } }` in the pi-envoy test), and the listener creates `s-<id>` with a filter over the followed topics but, on this evidence, not at a start that covers what those topics stored while the session was away. The red test is the committed script with the command above; it fails at this head and the control run shows the same window green on the released plugin.

failures.evidence: A genuine data race this change creates, reported by CI's `envoy-go-race` lane at the code head 1099510d (run 41018009099, job 123944941163): `WARNING: DATA RACE`, a write from `TestListenerDeliveryHandler_FanoutAllowsUntaggedPayload.func1` at packages/envoy/cmd/listener/main_test.go:3420 against a read at main_test.go:3812, both reached through `listenerTransport.RoundTrip` → `internal/session.Deliverer.Push/prompt` → `servePortWorkers.pushUntilSettled` → `pushWithBackoff` → `servePortWorkers.work` → `enqueue`, from two goroutines `handOverPush` (delivery.go:563) started. The racing value is the test harness's own counter, `deliveries := map[string]int{}` (main_test.go:3418), not production state, so no shipped code is wrong — but the race exists because this change gives each serving-port session its own worker (EV-14) where the push used to be inline and serial, so it is this change's to fix and `-race` is red on it. The fix is test-only: guard that counter (a mutex, or atomics per session) and check the sibling harnesses that count deliveries the same way. I did not write it myself: making a red test pass is the implementer's, and I would rather hand over a precise finding than edit the file it must change.
